results.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
results.proof_sketch: Let D={0,1,2}, where 2 means “at least two”, and define a⊕b=min(2,a+b) and a⊗b=min(2,ab). The map h(r)=min(2,r) from nonnegative integers to D preserves addition and multiplication under these saturated operations. Consequently, transfer-matrix products over D exactly distinguish zero, one, and multiple assignments. These are precisely the three cases needed by every uniqueness quantifier.

results.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
results.proof_sketch:
For column i, fix its local type-3 tuple x and type-2 tuple y. Define the 2×2 matrix A_i(x,y), indexed by incoming and outgoing carries β,γ∈{0,1}, whose entry is the saturated number of local type-1 tuples z satisfying the column equation. For fixed global x,y, starting with q_0=(1,0), the product recurrence q_i=q_{i-1}A_i(x_i,y_i) has q_i(γ) equal to the saturated number of type-1 assignments to the first i columns ending with carry γ. Thus ∃!v_1 holds exactly when q_m(α)=1, where α is the required final carry.

There are only |D^2|=9 possible q-states. For fixed local x, form a 9×9 matrix B_i(x) whose (p,q)-entry is the saturated number of local type-2 tuples y for which pA_i(x,y)=q. Starting with the unit vector d_0 concentrated at (1,0), the recurrence d_i=d_{i-1}B_i(x_i) counts, truncated at two, the type-2 prefixes reaching each q-state. Hence ∃!v_2:∃!v_1 holds exactly when the saturated sum of d_m(q) over q with q(α)=1 equals one.

Finally, d ranges over the constant set D^9 of size 3^9. At each column, add a layered edge d→dB_i(x) for every local type-3 tuple x. A path from d_0 to an accepting final state exists exactly when some global type-3 assignment satisfies the two nested uniqueness quantifiers. Each column has at most three variable cells total, so constructing all A_i and B_i examines at most n^3 combined local tuples. The remaining state-space factors are constants.

results.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is exactly a constant-state relational word problem after per-column normalization.
results.proof_sketch: Use the verified d-state space S=D^9, initial state d_0, and accepting set F_α={d: the saturated sum of d(q) over q(α)=1 is one}. Order columns least to most significant and define R_i⊆S×S by (d,e)∈R_i iff some assignment x to column i’s type-3 cells satisfies e=dB_i(x). A global type-3 assignment x_1,…,x_m determines the unique state sequence d_i=d_{i-1}B_i(x_i), hence an R_1⋯R_m path. Conversely, choose a witnessing local x_i for every edge of such a path; column cells are disjoint, so their union is a global type-3 assignment. The endpoint is in F_α exactly when the nested type-2/type-1 uniqueness condition holds. Therefore the original instance is YES iff R_1⋯R_m connects d_0 to F_α. This proves both directions needed to transfer conclusions from the relational formulation.

results.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
results.proof_sketch: Begin with the two carry states. Eliminating one globally unique digit track replaces an N-state automaton by a deterministic saturated-count automaton with 3^N states: its state records, for every old state, whether zero, one, or multiple assignments of the eliminated track reach it. Repeating this for type 1, then type 2, and so forth preserves exact nested-uniqueness semantics. For each fixed level k, the resulting tower-sized state set depends only on k, not on m or n; the outer type-k existential quantifier is ordinary layered reachability. Thus every fixed k has a polynomial-time algorithm, although the constant grows rapidly with k.

results.claim: Under the source paper’s polynomial-base convention and any uniform-AC0-decodable explicit-column encoding, every fixed-level additive restoration problem is in logspace-uniform NC1.
results.proof_sketch: Fix k and let S_k be the constant lifted state set. For each column and each pair s,t∈S_k, the predicate (s,t)∈R_i has a constant-depth, polynomial-size circuit: expose the column fields by the stated encoding, enumerate the polynomially many candidate digits (and pairs of candidates when testing whether a count is at least two), guard them by digit<n, test the O(log n)-bit addition equation with uniform AC0 addition, and unroll the fixed number of saturated-count lifts. The convention n≤N^{O(1)} makes this size polynomial in encoded length N, and O(log N)-bit counters uniformly generate the circuit. Represent R_i by its constant-dimensional Boolean matrix. A balanced tree of Boolean matrix products computes R_1⋯R_m in depth O(log m); one product layer has constant depth because |S_k| is constant. Testing the initial-to-accepting entries is constant depth. Hence the family has polynomial size, O(log N) depth, and logspace uniformity.

results.claim: Under the source paper’s polynomial encoding convention, every fixed-level additive restoration problem is decidable in deterministic logarithmic space; for every fixed base it is a regular column language.
results.proof_sketch: Let N be the encoded input length. The convention under which polynomial dependence on n is polynomial entails n≤N^{O(1)}, so log n=O(log N). For fixed k, every iterated saturated state set is a constant depending only on k. A deterministic machine stores the constant-size bitset R of states reachable after the processed columns. For each state in R and each local outer assignment, it reconstructs the lifted transition by enumerating assignments to the at most three cells in that column. At most three O(log n)-bit digit counters, an O(log m)-bit position counter, and constant-size saturated tables suffice. It writes the resulting states into the next constant-size bitset and finally applies the required carry acceptance test. Hence the workspace is O(log m+log n)=O(log N). If n and k are fixed, the column alphabet and the reachable-state update are both finite; incorporating the initial and final carries gives a finite automaton, so the column language is regular.

results.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this does not provide the requested meaningful matching hardness classification.
results.proof_sketch: The algorithm above gives membership in P. The language is nontrivial: in base 2 with final carry 0, the one-column puzzle x_3+0=0 is YES, while x_3+1=0 is NO. For any L∈P, a polynomial-time many-one reduction can decide its input and output the fixed YES or NO instance accordingly. This proves formal P-hardness under that reduction notion. But the argument applies to every nontrivial language in P precisely because the reduction decides L itself. It establishes neither logspace-reduction P-hardness nor another discriminating lower bound, so it does not satisfy the target’s matching-hardness requirement.

results.claim: Even in base 2 with no type-3 cells, level-3 additive restoration is ODD-PARITY-hard under constant-length projections, and therefore is not in AC0.
results.proof_sketch: Process columns from least to most significant and write U=(T1,T1,T1), I=(0,1,T1), and V=(0,1,T2). Map a bit word b_1…b_s to the base-2 puzzle U W_{b_1}…W_{b_s}, where W_0=II, W_1=VU, and the required final carry is 0. This is a two-column-per-bit projection. I acts identically on the saturated type-1 carry-count vector q. U has matrix [[2,1],[1,2]], so its prefix sends (1,0) to E=(2,1). Across VU, choosing V’s type-2 digit c sends (a,b) to (b,min(2,2b)) when c=0 and to (min(2,2a),a) when c=1. With O=(1,2) and M=(2,2), the transitions are E→O only for c=0, O→E only for c=1, every other choice enters M, and M is absorbing. Thus exactly one type-2 assignment avoids M, namely 0,1,0,1,… over the 1-bits. It ends in O, whose final-carry-0 count is one, exactly when the number of 1-bits is odd; E and M have count two. The empty type-3 block leaves this truth value unchanged. The standard PARITY lower bound for AC0 gives the conclusion.

results.claim: The meaningful classification is narrowed to a projection lower bound by ODD PARITY and a deterministic-logspace upper bound, but no matching hardness classification is established.
results.proof_sketch: The preceding two claims give ODD-PARITY ≤_proj Level-3-Additive-Restoration ∈ L under the source’s convention. In particular, the lower bound is nonvacuous and rules out AC0, unlike polynomial-time-many-one P-hardness. Conversely, if this language were P-hard under logspace many-one reductions, then every language in P could be decided in L by composing its reduction with the L decider; closure of L under such composition would imply P=L. This is a precise obstruction, not an unconditional separation and not a matching lower bound. No hardness for L or NC1 under reductions weaker than those classes is proved, so the requested matching classification remains open and the resolution remains PARTIAL.

results.claim: For uniform-AC0-decodable explicit-column encodings, the meaningful classification is narrowed to a projection lower bound by ODD PARITY and a logspace-uniform NC1 upper bound, but no matching hardness classification is established.
results.proof_sketch: The structural relation product gives Level-3-Additive-Restoration∈NC1 under the polynomial-base and AC0-decodable-encoding qualifications, while the explicit construction gives ODD-PARITY≤_proj Level-3-Additive-Restoration and excludes AC0. These endpoints do not match: parity hardness is not an NC1-hardness proof, and no reduction from an NC1-complete problem is supplied. Exact finite-monoid exploration of the base-2 automaton found only trivial and order-two maximal subgroups, so the tempting non-solvable-group route to an NC1 lower bound is unsupported; this computation is diagnostic, not a separation theorem. Formal P-hardness under polynomial-time reductions remains nondiscriminating. Thus neither NC1 completeness nor a sharper matching modular-circuit classification has been proved, and the requested matching-hardness component remains open.

final_writeup:
The level-3 additive meta-restoration problem has a sharper conditional upper bound than the audited draft stated: under the source paper’s convention that n is polynomially bounded in encoded length, and for any uniform-AC0-decodable explicit-column encoding, it is in logspace-uniform NC1. The audited O(mn^3) time and deterministic-logspace bounds remain valid with their audited source-convention qualification. The target is nevertheless only partially resolved because the best proved lower bound is parity, not matching NC1 hardness.

First truncate every nonnegative count to D={0,1,2}, with 2 meaning at least two. The saturation map preserves addition and multiplication, so it retains exactly the information used by uniqueness quantifiers. For fixed type-3 and type-2 digits, q∈D^2 records the saturated numbers of type-1 prefixes ending in the two carry states. After the next counting lift, d∈D^9 records the saturated numbers of type-2 prefixes reaching each q-state. The final predicate says that the saturated total over q with q(α)=1 is exactly one.

The structural reformulation is a constant-state relational word problem. Let S=D^9 and order columns least to most significant. For column i, put (d,e) in R_i when some local type-3 assignment x makes e=dB_i(x). Every global type-3 assignment determines an R_1⋯R_m path from the initial state, because each column update is deterministic after x is fixed. Conversely, witnesses for the edges of any such path combine into a global assignment because blanks in different columns are distinct. The endpoint is accepting exactly when there is a unique type-2 assignment having a unique type-1 completion. Thus the reformulation is equivalent in both directions, including the final carry condition.

This equivalence yields the conditional NC1 refinement. For fixed states d,e, a polynomial-size constant-depth circuit computes whether (d,e)∈R_i. The assumed encoding exposes each column’s fields in uniform AC0. The circuit enumerates all candidate local digits in parallel, tests the binary addition equation, and represents a saturated count by the predicates “at least one” and “at least two”; the latter is an OR over pairs of distinct witnesses. There are only three cells in a column and only two fixed counting lifts at level 3. Binary addition is in uniform AC0, and n≤N^{O(1)} under the stated convention, so every local relation has a uniform constant-depth polynomial-size circuit. Representing each R_i as a constant-dimensional Boolean matrix, a balanced product tree composes all m relations in O(log m) depth and polynomial size. Initial and accepting states are then tested in constant depth. The same argument works for every fixed level k: the lifted state set and number of unrolled counting layers depend on k but not on the input.

The saturated state is essential. A carry-only graph that retains merely locally unique transitions is unsound: with two base-2 columns, all six cells type 1, and final carry 0, the locally unique carry path 0→1→0 coexists with nine fillings through intermediate carry 0, for ten global fillings total. Saturated count vectors correctly reject this instance. For fixed base and level, the normalized column alphabet and state set are finite, so the language is regular.

The parity lower bound is preserved exactly. In base 2 with no type-3 cells, let U=(T1,T1,T1), I=(0,1,T1), and V=(0,1,T2). Prefix by U; encode bit 0 as II and bit 1 as VU; require final carry 0. U creates E=(2,1). A VU block has one type-2 digit: from E only 0 avoids the absorbing state M=(2,2) and reaches O=(1,2), while from O only 1 avoids M and returns to E. Hence exactly one type-2 assignment remains viable, and its type-1 completion is unique at final carry 0 exactly after an odd number of input 1s. This is a constant-length projection from ODD PARITY, so the problem is not in AC0.

Consequently, for uniform-AC0-decodable explicit-column encodings, the substantive bracket sharpens to ODD-PARITY-hard under projections and membership in logspace-uniform NC1; the audited upper bound remains L under the source convention. The formal polynomial-time-many-one P-completeness statement is still true but nondiscriminating, because such a reduction may decide its source language and select fixed YES/NO instances. Parity hardness does not establish NC1 hardness, and the structural search supplied no valid reduction from an NC1-complete language or matching modular-circuit upper classification. The requested matching hardness result therefore remains unresolved, so claimed_resolution remains PARTIAL.
